GUIDE

Voltage Amps Watts Calculator — Watt's Law Guide

DC circuit loop

Battery voltage and current converted directly into watts

DC pages need a clean loop: battery, load, current direction, and watts without power factor.

Formula P = V x I

Quick answer

Use this calculator when DC current and voltage convert directly into watts.

DC systems do not use power factor, so the calculation is direct. This is useful for batteries, automotive systems, LED drivers, electronics, and solar DC accessories.

P = V x I

Inputs to check before calculating

  • Use measured voltage when battery voltage is above or below nominal.
  • Enter continuous current for heat and runtime planning.
  • Check fuse and wire ratings against the calculated current.
  • For battery loads, convert watts into Wh for runtime estimates.

Example: 10 amps at 120 volts

At 120 volts, 10 amps equals 1,200 watts before AC power-factor adjustments. Formula: 10 A x 120 V = 1,200 W.

Best use cases

  • Find watts from V and A
  • Clear formula context
  • General electrical planning
  • DC load planning with clear unit labels.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not assume a 12V battery is always exactly 12.0V; charging and resting voltage can change the watt result.

How to use the result

Use the watt output to compare loads, size power supplies, and estimate battery energy use.

Accuracy and safety note

Calculator output is a planning estimate. Final breaker sizing, wire gauge, derating, voltage-drop limits, equipment protection, and code compliance should be verified with manufacturer documentation and a qualified electrician or engineer.

For the broad formula, reference table, and breaker planning context, start with the main Amps to Watts Calculator.

Voltage Amps Watts Calculator Guide
VAW

How the Voltage Amps Watts Calculator Works

A voltage amps watts calculator calculates watts, amps, or volts when two electrical values are known. The calculator uses voltage, electric current, amperage, electrical power, wattage, resistance, and power factor to solve common electrical equations.

Use this electrical conversion calculator for household power calculation, circuit load calculation, generator sizing, inverter watt calculation, battery power calculation, solar power calculation, electrical appliance wattage, and power supply calculation.

V/A

Volts Amps Watts Calculator

A volts amps watts calculator shows the amps volts watts relationship in one place. Voltage is electrical pressure in volts, current is charge flow in amperes, and watts measure real electrical power used by the load.

The same calculator can work as an amps to watts calculator, watts to amps calculator, volts to watts calculator, voltage current watts calculator, and voltage amperage wattage calculator.

VoltageVolt (V)CurrentAmpere (A)PowerWatt (W)
FORM

Watt Voltage Amp Formula

The watt voltage amp formula is W = V x A for DC and power factor 1.00 loads. Rearranged formulas are A = W / V and V = W / A. These formulas support calculate amps from watts, calculate watts from volts, and current draw formula searches.

Watts = Volts x Amps
Amps = Watts / Volts
Volts = Watts / Amps
OHM

Volts Amps Watts Ohms Calculator

A volts amps watts ohms calculator combines Ohm's Law and the electrical power formula. Ohm's Law uses V = I x R, where voltage equals current times resistance. Power formulas use W = V x A, W = A² x Ω, and W = V² / Ω.

Use resistance in ohms (Ω) when the electrical circuit has a known resistor, heater, conductor, wire gauge, or load resistance.

RES

Volts Amps Watts Resistance Calculator

A volts amps watts resistance calculator finds resistance, current, voltage, or power from known values. Use R = V / A to calculate resistance, A = V / R to calculate current, and W = A² x R to calculate heating power.

Resistance matters in copper wire, aluminum wire, conductors, transformers, heating elements, speaker coils, and voltage drop calculations.

W

How to Determine Watts from Amps and Volts

To determine watts from amps and volts, multiply amps by volts. For example, 5 amps at 120 volts equals 600 watts. For AC loads with power factor, multiply volts x amps x power factor.

Formula: watts = volts x amps for DC. Formula: real watts = RMS voltage x amps x power factor for AC single-phase power.

A?

Can You Calculate Amps From Watts

Yes, you can calculate amps from watts when voltage is known. Use amps = watts / volts for DC loads and unity power factor loads. Use amps = watts / (volts x power factor) for AC single-phase loads.

This amp draw calculation is used for circuit breaker checks, battery amp calculation, inverter current draw, generator watt calculation, and wire ampacity calculation.

A=W/V

How to Calculate Amps from Watts

To calculate amp from watts, divide watts by volts. A 1,200W appliance at 120V draws 10A. A 1,200W appliance at 240V draws 5A when power factor is 1.00.

Use this formula for amps calculator from watts and volts, amp calculator watts volts, and how to get amperage from watts and volts queries.

V→W

How to Calculate Watts from Volts

To calculate watts from volts, multiply volts by amps. Voltage alone does not determine wattage. A 12V circuit at 10A equals 120W, while a 240V circuit at 10A equals 2,400W.

This watt calculation is useful for electrical measurements, power consumption, household power usage, electrical efficiency, and energy usage calculation.

VA

Voltage Amps to Watts Calculator

A voltage amps to watts calculator converts voltage and amperage into wattage. For DC, watts equal volts x amps. For AC, real power in watts can be lower than apparent power when power factor is below 1.00.

Apparent power is measured in volt-amperes (VA) or kilovolt-amperes (kVA). Real power is measured in watts or kilowatts. Reactive power is part of AC systems with motors, transformers, and inductive loads.

VAW

Volt Amps to Watts Calculator

A volt amps to watts calculator changes apparent power into real power when power factor is known. Use watts = VA x power factor. For example, 1,000VA at 0.80 power factor equals 800W.

This calculation matters for transformers, generators, inverters, uninterruptible power supplies, motors, and AC electrical load calculation.

AC

AC Volts Amps Watts Calculator

An AC volts amps watts calculator uses root mean square (RMS) voltage, current, and power factor. Single-phase AC power calculation uses W = V x A x PF. Three-phase power calculation uses W = 1.732 x V x A x PF for line-to-line voltage.

AC calculations support household loads, Australia 240V circuits, United States 120V and 240V circuits, generators, transformers, circuit breakers, and wire ampacity checks.

DC

DC Volt Amp Watt Calculator

A DC volt amp watt calculator uses W = V x A. DC has no power factor. DC power calculation applies to batteries, solar panels, LED drivers, automotive systems, amplifiers, DC motors, and electronics.

For example, 30W at 12V equals 2.5A. A 12V battery supplying 10A delivers 120W before losses.

3-Phase

Volts Amps Watts Calculator 3 Phase

A volts amps watts calculator 3 phase uses W = 1.732 x V x A x PF for line-to-line voltage. Three-phase power is used for motors, pumps, HVAC equipment, industrial panels, generators, and large electrical loads.

Example: 30A at 400V 3 phase with PF 0.90 equals 18,706W, or 18.7kW.

240

Volts Amps Watts Calculator 240V

A volts amps watts calculator 240V uses 240 volts as the circuit voltage. At 240V, 10A equals 2,400W, 20A equals 4,800W, and 30A equals 7,200W for DC or power factor 1.00 loads.

240V calculations are common for appliances, heaters, EV chargers, Australia circuits, UK circuits, and split-phase loads.

12V

Volts Amps Watts Calculator 12V

A volts amps watts calculator 12V uses 12 volts for battery, automotive, LED, amplifier, and solar loads. At 12V, 5A equals 60W, 10A equals 120W, and 30W equals 2.5A.

12V systems need careful voltage drop checks. Small voltage losses can reduce available load voltage.

AU

Volts Amps Watts Calculator Australia

A volts amps watts calculator Australia should support 230V and 240V single-phase circuits and 400V three-phase systems. Australian users often calculate appliance wattage, generator size, inverter power, solar panel current, and circuit load values.

For final electrical work, use the applicable Australian wiring rules and verify conductor size, circuit breaker rating, and voltage drop.

LOAD

Voltage Amp Power Calculator

A voltage amp power calculator converts voltage and amperage into electrical power. Use it to estimate power consumption, current draw, circuit load, energy usage, and kilowatt-hour (kWh) cost.

Energy consumption is kWh = watts x hours / 1,000. A 1,500W load running 4 hours uses 6kWh.

AMP

How Many Watts Does an Amplifier Use

An amplifier uses input watts based on output power, efficiency, voltage, and listening level. A 500W audio amplifier can draw more than 500W from the power supply when losses are included.

For a 12V car amplifier, current is approximately watts / volts / efficiency. A 500W amplifier at 12V and 80% efficiency draws about 52.1A.

1A

How Many Watts Can 1 Amp Handle

One amp can handle watts equal to the circuit voltage. At 5V, 1A equals 5W. At 12V, 1A equals 12W. At 120V, 1A equals 120W. At 240V, 1A equals 240W.

Circuit breaker size, wire gauge, American Wire Gauge (AWG), copper wire, aluminum wire, conductor insulation, and National Electrical Code (NEC) or International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) rules limit real installations.

FAQ

Voltage Amps Watts Calculator FAQ

Voltage amps watts calculator FAQ answers common power conversion questions directly. Use these answers for fast checks before using the interactive calculator.

Q1

Can you calculate amps from watts?

Yes, calculate amps from watts by dividing watts by volts. For AC loads, divide watts by volts x power factor.

Q2

What is the electrical power formula?

The electrical power formula is W = V x A. For AC single phase, real power is W = V x A x PF. For 3 phase, real power is W = 1.732 x V x A x PF.

Q3

How many amps is 10000 watts?

10,000 watts equals 83.33A at 120V, 45.45A at 220V, and 41.67A at 240V. Use power factor for AC real-world loads.

Q4

How do you get amperage from watts and volts?

Get amperage from watts and volts with A = W / V. Example: 2,400W / 240V = 10A.

Q5

How many watts is 5 volts 3 amps?

5 volts and 3 amps equals 15 watts. Use W = V x A, so 5 x 3 = 15W.

Q6

What is the difference between real power and apparent power?

Real power is watts, while apparent power is volt-amperes. Power factor connects both values with W = VA x PF.

Q7

Does power factor change amps?

Yes, lower power factor increases current for the same real watts. Motors, transformers, and some power supplies need power factor calculation.

Q8

Can this calculator size a circuit breaker?

No, this calculator gives electrical power and current values for planning. Circuit breaker sizing needs load type, continuous load rules, wire ampacity, temperature derating, voltage drop, and code checks.

FAQ

V A W FAQ

Fast answers before you use the calculator or compare formulas.

W How do I convert 120V amps to watts?

Multiply the current in amps by 120 volts. For example, 5 amps at 120V equals 600 watts (5 × 120 = 600). DC conversions do not require a power factor because current and voltage are always in phase.

BAT How many watts can a 120V battery deliver?

A 120V battery's power output depends on current draw. At 10A, it delivers 1200W. At 20A, it delivers 2400W. The maximum safe current depends on the battery's internal resistance, terminal rating, and fuse protection. Always check the battery data sheet for maximum discharge rate.

DC Why is DC conversion simpler than AC?

DC circuits have no power factor because current and voltage don't alternate. The formula is simply Watts = Amps × Volts. AC circuits have reactive power from inductors and capacitors that requires a power factor correction, making the formula Watts = Amps × Volts × PF.

AWG What wire gauge do I need for 120V DC?

Wire gauge for 120V DC depends on current, distance, and acceptable voltage drop. Low-voltage DC circuits are especially sensitive to voltage drop because a 0.5V loss is a larger percentage of 120V than of 120V. Use the wire gauge calculator with one-way distance and 120V to find the right conductor size.

PV Can I use this calculator for solar panel circuits?

Yes, but use the correct voltage point. Solar panels operate at Vmp (maximum power voltage), not the battery voltage. A 12V-nominal panel may have Vmp of 17–18V. For battery-side current, use the battery voltage. For panel-side wiring, use the panel Vmp.

RUN How do I calculate battery runtime from watts at 120V?

First convert amps to watts (A × 120V). Then convert battery capacity: Watt-hours = Amp-hours × 120V. Divide Wh by the load watts to estimate runtime in hours. Account for inverter efficiency (typically 85–92%) if converting DC to AC. Use the amp-hours to watt-hours calculator for detailed estimates.
